pages.title: Shell: the window and its rail
pages.note: The frame every view sits in: the brand, the views, what is coming from the KIV and the Observatory, the four ways to speak to everyone, and the portal's state at the foot. It matters because it is what Kris sees first and last: the portal line answers "are both Macs here?" on every page.
fields: Brand: the meeting ring, "Agora", which Mac this is
Views: Home, Who's doing what, What's being said, Broadcasts, Waits on you, Macs and the portal, Checkouts, each with a count where one helps
Later: Inbox (from the KIV), Insight (from the Observatory), shown but not yet live
Speak to everyone: Broadcast…, Away… (I'm back while away), Ping, Mark all
The portal: the two Macs and whether the portal is open, with when the other was last heard

pages.title: Shell: the tray
pages.note: The menu-bar menu, the quiet everyday face of Agora (DESIGN-2). The app opens from its first line. It matters because most days Kris only ever sees this: two lines must say whether all is well.
fields: Line 1: agents and Macs heard from
Line 2: All well, or how many need a look
Exception rows: at most 3, each with what Agora saw, what it did, at most two actions
Speak to everyone
Detail one level down: Agents, Macs and checkouts, Runs, Broadcasts, News
Agora itself: Sync now, Open log, About, Quit

pages.title: Home
pages.note: What is happening within each Agora and across them, at a glance: who is here, what needs a look, what waits on Kris and what was just said. It matters because it is the page the app opens on; every other view is a closer look at one of its panels.
fields: Summary: agents on Macs, how many need a look, how many queries wait
Who is here: each Mac with its agents, listening or not, and the portal
Needs a look: the same exceptions as the tray
Waits on you: the oldest queries, with their agent and focus
Just said: the last few things said, with layer (Git or Agora) and whether heard

pages.title: Who's doing what
pages.note: Every live agent on both Macs, what each looks after, whether it listens, and what waits on Kris; and the address book for routing by focus. It matters because routing an idea to the right agent depends on it, and because listening is shown from answers, not from what an agent says of itself.
fields: Agent: work id and title
Mac (as the group row)
Territory
Focus areas, primary first (★)
Listening: how (Agora's call, polling, on open, off) and last answer
Waits on you: count and first ids

pages.title: An agent
pages.note: One agent closer up: its focus areas with what each covers, its listening over the last two hours, the run and doers with it now, what was said with it, and its queries. It matters when an agent goes silent or holds many queries: everything needed to act is on one page.
fields: Focus areas with descriptions
Listening: method, recent answers, next check
With it now: run, doers, checkouts
Said with it: last hour, both directions
Waits on you: query, what, focus, since, recommended answer

pages.title: What's being said
pages.note: Everything said between agents and to Kris on both Macs, newest first, in both layers. It matters because "everyone hears" is Agora's first goal: this is where Kris sees what was said and whether it was heard. It is a record to look along, not a chat.
fields: Time
From → to
Kind: message, call, broadcast, ping, mark, health, pushed
Layer: Git (durable) or Agora (conversational)
What was said, in a line
Heard: when, or silent

pages.title: Broadcasts
pages.note: What Kris said to everyone, and who heard it. It matters because a broadcast such as Away opens an unattended window: Kris needs to know every agent took it.
fields: Sent
What
Kind: message, away, back, ping, mark
Heard: answered of reached
Silent: who did not answer
For the selected one: each agent, answered or silent

pages.title: Waits on you
pages.note: Every query waiting on Kris across all agents, gathered in one place. It matters because these are the decisions only Kris can make, and today they sit in ten separate discussions files.
fields: Query id
What, in a line
Focus
Since
Recommended answer
Agent

pages.title: Macs and the portal
pages.note: The two Macs and the portal between them: presence, where each listens, its Agora, agents and checkouts, and what crossed the portal this hour. It matters when something is not getting across.
fields: Per Mac: presence, address, Agora version and uptime, agents, checkouts, last review
The portal: network, last heard and round trip, traffic this hour, queued, state swapped

pages.title: Checkouts
pages.note: Every kept checkout on both Macs, side by side, showing only those not level by default. It matters because "everyone is level" is Agora's second goal, and a diverged checkout blocks an agent.
fields: Repository
Condition on sol
Condition on terra
Whether the Macs agree
For the selected one: what Agora did and who was called

artboards.title: Rail expanded, terra not heard from
The two squares
artboards.why: It answers "who is here, on which Mac, and is the portal open" in one look, carries the identity (the meeting ring on each Mac, the portal Kris described) and keeps the stream of words short.
artboards.gains: The two places and the portal are visible; silent and on-open agents stand out by shape; one look answers the home question.
artboards.costs: The picture takes space and crowds past about 12 agents a Mac; it needs the table (2.1) as its text equivalent.

artboards.title: Figures and a table
artboards.gains: Densest; scales to many agents; nothing to learn.
artboards.costs: No sense of two places or the portal; repeats 2.1 almost exactly; reads like a dashboard of numbers.

artboards.title: What's being said first
artboards.gains: Feels alive; shows the conversation that Agora carries.
artboards.costs: A feed asks to be watched, against "navigation over consumption"; what needs a look and what waits on Kris drop out of sight.

artboards.title: By Mac
artboards.why: Rows stay where Kris learnt them (by Mac, territory, work id), listening and queries read across each row, and the address book is one search away in the same view.
artboards.gains: Stable order; every fact about an agent on one row; the selected agent's detail below without leaving the page.
artboards.costs: Finding who covers a focus needs the search box; an agent with many focus areas wraps.

artboards.title: By focus: the address book
artboards.gains: Routing by focus is the primary act; shared focus areas and their primary owner show at once.
artboards.costs: An agent appears on several rows; listening and queries are per focus, not per agent; weak for "is everyone here?".

artboards.title: ki.prj.agora
artboards.why: One page holds everything needed to act on one agent, with the single brass action for what waits on Kris.
artboards.gains: Complete; the listening bars make a lapse obvious.
artboards.costs: Long for an agent with many queries; the bars need a legend.

artboards.title: One record, newest first
artboards.why: One record with a layer column and filters keeps the order of events, which matters when a push, a call and a reply follow one another across the portal.
artboards.gains: Time order is kept across layers; filters narrow to Git or Agora, one Mac or both.
artboards.costs: Busy hours make it long; the layer is a column, not a place.

artboards.title: By layer
artboards.gains: Teaches the two layers: what was written to the record and what was only said.
artboards.costs: Breaks the order of events across the two columns; a push and the call it causes sit apart.

artboards.title: Sent and heard
artboards.why: Pairs each broadcast with who heard it, and offers the one useful next step: ping the silent again.
artboards.gains: Answers "did everyone take the Away?" directly.
artboards.costs: Received broadcasts from terra need their own section below.

artboards.title: By agent
artboards.why: Kris answers a query in its agent's thread, so grouping by agent matches where the answer goes; oldest first within each keeps the longest-waiting at the top.
artboards.gains: Matches how queries are answered; each agent's load is visible.
artboards.costs: The oldest query overall can sit under a later agent; switch to Oldest first to see it.

artboards.title: Oldest first, all together
artboards.gains: The longest wait is always at the top; good for a morning sweep.
artboards.costs: Jumps between agents row to row; related queries (all of SCHED-) scatter.

artboards.title: The two Macs and the portal
artboards.why: The same two squares as home, with each Mac and the portal as a small table of facts below it.
artboards.gains: Facts sit under the picture they belong to.

artboards.title: Not level, side by side
artboards.why: Both Macs side by side make a disagreement plain, and showing only what is not level keeps the page short.
artboards.gains: Disagreements stand out; what Agora did is beside the checkout.
artboards.costs: A Mac that carries a repository the other does not needs a dash.
